Overview

Muscat as a Business Centre

Muscat is the capital of the Sultanate of Oman and its principal commercial centre. The National Centre for Statistics and Information recorded a registered population of about 1.55 million in Muscat Governorate at the end of July 2026, out of roughly 5.4 million nationally, and the governorate has the highest population density in the country. Seeb has the largest Omani population of any wilayat, while Bausher has the highest share of expatriate residents. The city hosts the ministries, the central bank, the national stock exchange and capital markets regulator, the head offices of the main banks and state-linked investment and energy companies, and many regional offices of international contractors.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Muscat because access to Omani projects, licences and state-linked buyers usually runs through the capital. Foreign companies appointing local partners, agents or sponsors need to understand who owns them and whether they are connected to officials or influential families. Energy, logistics, tourism and infrastructure investment under the national development agenda brings joint ventures and supply contracts that require integrity checks. Corporate records and court files are not as openly searchable as in some markets, so careful use of available registry information, published decisions and Arabic and English media is needed, together with on-the-ground enquiries by qualified local professionals.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Muscat

01

Local partner and agent diligence

Foreign companies entering Oman often work with Muscat-based partners, commercial agents or joint venture companies. We review commercial registration information, shareholders and managers, connected companies, litigation and Arabic and English media to identify ultimate control, links to officials or prominent families and any history of disputes.

02

Energy and infrastructure supply chains

Oil, gas, power, water and infrastructure projects are commissioned and managed from Muscat by state-linked companies. Contractors and subcontractors seeking these projects can carry integrity and performance risks. We research ownership, prior awards, disputes and adverse media so clients can meet anti-corruption and supplier due diligence obligations.

03

Investment and Commerce Court support

Shareholder, banking, insurance, insolvency and investment contract disputes now go to the Investment and Commerce Court, headquartered in Muscat, with a target of judgment within ninety days of referral. That pace leaves little time to prepare, so we support counsel early with counterparty histories, corporate structures and asset leads.

04

Listed company and investor screening

Investors in Muscat Stock Exchange companies, private placements or family businesses seeking capital need to understand controlling shareholders and related-party dealings. We combine disclosures, registry information, regulatory notices and media to map ownership and relationships and to highlight governance issues before investment or board appointments.

05

Executive and senior hire backgrounds

Regional headquarters and state-linked companies in Muscat recruit senior executives from across the Gulf and beyond. We verify career and qualification claims, review litigation, regulatory and media records in the countries where candidates have worked, and observe Oman's Personal Data Protection Law and counsel's advice on consent.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Muscat

Investment and Commerce Court

A Royal Decree issued on 23 March 2025 established the Investment and Commerce Court, which began operating on 1 October 2025 with its headquarters in Muscat under the Supreme Judicial Council. It has exclusive competence where at least one party is a merchant and the dispute concerns commercial business, and over investment contract disputes, covering shareholder, banking, securities, insurance, insolvency, intellectual property and public-private partnership matters. Circuits are expected to decide cases within ninety days of referral, with tight deadlines for filings and limited postponements.

Court circuits beyond Muscat

Supreme Judicial Council Decision 433/2025 set up primary and appellate circuits of the court across the governorates, including appellate circuits in Dhofar, Al Dakhiliyah, North Al Batinah and North Al Sharqiyah and primary circuits in ten governorates. Matters involving Muscat counterparties may therefore be heard at the headquarters or in a regional circuit depending on territorial jurisdiction, which counsel should confirm. Proceedings are in Arabic, and court records are not generally searchable by the public.

Registries and the chamber

Commercial registration is administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion in Muscat, and registration details such as company name, legal form, activities and listed partners can generally be obtained, with third-party access varying. Beneficial ownership registers kept under the 2023 regulation are not publicly available. The Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry, headquartered in Muscat, supports the Oman Commercial Arbitration Centre, which administers institutional arbitration.

Financial regulators in the capital

The Central Bank of Oman supervises banks and the Financial Services Authority oversees the capital market, insurance and the Muscat Stock Exchange, all based in Muscat. Their circulars, enforcement notices and listed company disclosures are useful public sources for understanding a financial counterparty's regulatory history and the shareholdings of listed companies and their major investors. Where a counterparty is regulated, we check these sources alongside court and media research.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Muscat

TDSC has no office in Muscat and works on Muscat matters from its Nashville headquarters. We first define the client's decision, such as appointing an agent, joining a project consortium, investing in a listed or family company or preparing for proceedings in the Investment and Commerce Court, and agree with Omani counsel which sources may lawfully be used and how the Personal Data Protection Law applies. Questions

Muscat: Frequently Asked Questions

Which court hears commercial disputes in Muscat?

Since 1 October 2025, commercial disputes where at least one party is a merchant, and investment contract disputes, fall under the Investment and Commerce Court, headquartered in Muscat under the Supreme Judicial Council. Regional circuits also exist. Administrative, labour and rental disputes are excluded. Omani counsel confirms jurisdiction and which circuit applies to a particular matter.

How quickly do cases move in the new court?

The court's rules target a judgment within ninety days of referral, with short, fixed windows for defendants' filings and limited postponements. New documents after those windows need the court's permission. In practice this means background research, corporate mapping and asset leads should be ready before proceedings start, not gathered while they are running.

Can you find out who owns a Muscat company?

Commercial registration information from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion generally shows legal form, activities and listed partners or shareholders, and listed companies disclose major shareholders. Beneficial ownership registers are not public, so we combine registry data with disclosures, media and local enquiries, stating clearly where ownership is inferred.

Do you check links between Omani partners and officials?

Yes, using lawful open sources. We look for family, business and appointment connections between a partner's owners and public officials or state-linked companies, relevant to Oman's public funds and conflict of interest rules and to foreign anti-bribery laws. We do not use pretexting or access restricted government systems.

Does TDSC have staff in Oman?

No. TDSC is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Oman. We have not identified a licensing regime for private investigators in Oman, so any work in Muscat is carried out by qualified local professionals we coordinate, with Omani counsel confirming what may lawfully be done.
